chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn al-Khazraj, that he wrote to him

A man sent a proposal to a man, so the days were prolonged with it, and the months, and the years. So he wondered if he should say to him, 'Do it', or 'Have you done it'? So he answered with regards to it: 'It is not Obligatory upon him except what his heart is tied down with, and about which his decision is established'.

key_terms.عَقَدَ عَلَيْهِ قَلْبَهُ: His heart was tied to it

ai.seo_question: When does a marriage proposal become binding in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Imam clarifies that a prolonged marriage proposal (*khitbah*) remains revocable, establishing that binding obligation arises only from firm internal resolve (*thabat al-'azimah*) rather than the mere passage of time. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that *khitbah* is a pre-contractual stage distinct from the actual marriage contract (*aqd*), allowing flexibility before mutual consent is finalized. It underscores the importance of psychological commitment over procedural delay in Islamic family law.
